title: WHAT IF THEY DO NOT BELIEVE ME?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses answered, "What if they do not believe me or listen to me and say, 'The Lord did not appear to you'?"" - Exodus 4:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God has just given Moses a clear commission and an unshakeable promise. Moses responds with a fear that many of us know well: what if nobody believes me?

He is not imagining things. He had been rejected by his own people once before, forty years earlier, and that memory has not faded. Old wounds shape new fears.

Notice that God does not scold him for asking. In the verses that follow, God patiently gives him signs. Our God is remarkably gentle with genuine fear, even when that fear is mixed with unbelief.

But notice also what Moses is doing. He is making his obedience conditional on other people's response. That is a trap. If I only obey God when I am confident people will receive it, I will rarely obey at all.

Jesus was rejected by many who saw His miracles with their own eyes (Jn 12:37). Faithfulness is measured by obedience, not by how people react to it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is fear of rejection stopping me from obeying God?
2. What old wound is shaping how I read today's situation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know my fear of being dismissed. Help me to obey You faithfully and leave people's responses in Your hands. Amen.
